Fastest next year, Apple will launch its first smart glasses equipped with artificial intelligence. The glasses will integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri into the real world. Here is what we expect.

Core Features

First, these glasses are AI glasses, not augmented reality (AR) glasses. In other words, they mainly operate via voice and camera, as they will not come with any display screen.

The camera will let Siri observe your real-world surroundings, answer questions, provide information, and translate signs. We also expect the glasses to include a feature that lets you ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you later. This feature was first exposed in a data leak from macOS 26.7.

They will also come with speakers for playing music and sound effects, so you can think of them as open-ear headphones.

However, according to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, these glasses may not be able to take photos and record videos like a typical camera. Meta’s Ray-Ban smart glasses have recently caused huge privacy controversies, and Apple may want to avoid repeating the same mistakes.

Design Styles

Unlike Meta, Apple has not partnered with an existing eyewear manufacturer to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, the company is designing them in-house and is developing several different styles:

Larger rectangular frames, reminiscent of the Ray-Ban Wayfarer; a slimmer rectangular design, similar to the glasses worn by Apple CEO Tim Cook; larger oval or round frames; smaller, more refined oval or round styles.

The glasses are reportedly made of acetate, which is more durable than plastic and looks more premium. Apple will offer several color options, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.

Health Features

According to reports, Apple is considering positioning the product as a health device in future versions. This may mean adding heart-rate monitoring (similar to AirPods Pro 3), as well as more software features (such as Workout Buddy on Apple Watch), to make the device more useful.

Beyond that, how Apple will make these features work for health remains unknown—though for the first generation, don’t hold your breath.

Release Date

Recent reports suggest that Apple will unveil these glasses at WWDC 2027, giving developers time to prepare in advance. The product will then go on sale at the end of the same year, most likely in September, alongside the 20th-anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more here.

Are you excited about Apple’s first smart glasses? Let us know in the comments.
